description.narrative:
ASEAN Youth Organization (AYO) is an international non-partisan, non-profit, and non-governmental organization established to promote international understanding and goodwill parallel to the ASEAN Motto and constitutes one vision, identity, and community.
Our vision is to create a world where youths exhibit a heightened interest in ASEAN through our activities that Empower Youth, Engage, <(>&<)> Educate Communities to implement ideas that enable Positive Sustainable Change.
With 10 years of experience inCommunity Development, ASEAN Youth Organization provides Youth with knowledge, skills, and abilities to bring back to their communities, as well as boosting the regional development by fostering partnerships with various stakeholders.
AYO is going to implement "The ASEAN Youth Sustainability Forum (AYSF) 2026" was developed by ASEAN Youth Organization Environment (AYO Enviro) to address the growing challengeof climate injustice across Southeast Asia. While climate change affects all communities, its impacts are disproportionately felt by vulnerable groups, including low-income communities, women, indigenous peoples, and youth, despite their limited contribution to greenhouse gas emissions. The project responds to the need for greater youth participation in climate decision-making and stronger regional collaboration on sustainable development. The concept was developed through AYO Enviro's ongoing engagement with youth networks, environmental advocates, academic institutions, and community organizations across ASEAN. Drawing on lessons from previous ASEANYouth Organization initiatives and increasing calls for inclusive climate action, AYSF 2026 was designed as a regional platform combining policy dialogue, experiential learning, and youth-led solution development. The forum aims to strengthen climate literacy, leadership, and cross-border cooperation among young people while ensuring that climate action is both equitable and inclusive.
AYSF 2026 adopts a rights-based, youth-led, experiential, andnetwork-driven approach to strengthening climate justice leadership among young people across ASEAN. The Forum recognizes youth as key stakeholders in climate action and sustainable development, whose meaningful participation is essential to achieving inclusive and equitable solutions to the region's environmental challenges. At the core of the approach is a rights-based framework that promotes participation, inclusion, accountability, and equity. The Forum creates opportunities for youth to engage directly with policymakers, practitioners, academics, and community representatives, ensuring that diverse perspectives—including those of women, marginalized communities, and underrepresented groups—are reflected in climate justicediscussions and solution development. The Forum combines expert dialogue with experiential learning opportunities, including site visits, interactive workshops, mentorship sessions, and collaborative group activities. This approach enables participants to connectclimate justice concepts with real-world challenges, strengthening both their understanding and their capacity to develop practical, locally relevant solutions. AYSF 2026 also adopts a youth leadership and peer-learning approach that recognizes young people as active contributors to social change rather than passive beneficiaries. Through leadership development, collaborative problem-solving,and cross-cultural exchange, participants strengthen their knowledge, confidence, and ability to contribute to climate action within their communities and organizations.
To promote sustainability beyond the event itself, the Forum strengthens regional networks among youth leaders, civil society organizations, academic institutions, and development partners. These connections provide ongoing opportunities for knowledge sharing, collaboration, and joint action, supporting continued engagement on climate justice issues after the Forum concludes. This approach builds on lessons from previous ASEAN Youth Organization initiatives, which have demonstrated that combining experiential learning, mentorship, and regional networking creates stronger and more sustainable outcomes than stand-alone awareness-raising activities. By strengthening individual leadership capacities while fosteringregional collaboration, AYSF 2026 seeks to generate lasting impacts that extend beyond the Forum and contribute to a more inclusive and youth-driven climate movement across ASEAN.

participating-org.narrative:
ASEAN Youth Organization is an international non-partisan, non-profit, and non-governmental organization established to promote international understanding and goodwill parallel to the ASEAN Motto and constitutes one vision, identity, and community.
Our vision is to create a world where youths exhibit a heightened interest in ASEAN through our activities that Empower Youth, Engage, <(>&<)> Educate Communities to implement ideas that enable Positive Sustainable Change.
With 10 years of experience in Community Development, ASEAN Youth Organization provides Youth with knowledge, skills, and abilities to bring back to their communities, as well as boosting the regional development by fostering partnerships with various stakeholders. ASEAN Youth Organizationwas initiated and founded in 2013 by Senjaya Mulia from Indonesia. This initiation arose because Senjaya was part of the ASEAN Community Facebook Page, an online platform managed by youths from ASEAN countries and shared about ASEAN Cultures.
In 2018,AYO received the ASEAN emblem and nameauthorization from the ASEAN Secretariat and established the AYO Social Enterprise (AYOSE) in Indonesia (Headquarter) and 2 branches in Philippines and Singapore.
AYOSE established other arm's organizations to support its sustainability: AYO Academy, AYO Enviro,AYO Recent, and AYO Post.
Senjaya Mulia initiated the establishment of the ASEAN Youth Organization (AYO) in 2012. He also registered the organization as foundation and Social Enterprise to support theorganization's sustainability in 2015.
With the support of the solid team, AYO operates in All ASEAN Member states and become the largest youth network in ASEAN and beyond. Under the AYO Social Enterprise, Senjaya and his team also established other institutions such as AYO Academy, AYO Research Center, AYO Enviro, and AYOPost.
ASEAN Youth Organization is proud to be a platform to make your voices heard, where youth's aspirations are transformed intosustainable impact and a melting pot of different cultural, developmental and social aspirations of the youth.
AYO emphasizes on youth leading the youth and welcome everyone who has a burning desire to transform and uplift their community to be a part of AYO journey.
